Subject: Performance benchmark readout — scheduling

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for running the evals with our Dedicated preview. The engineering team at Acme asked for a short readout to walk through the latency and throughput numbers, confirm the test setup, and align on next steps for procurement.

Who from your side should join? You mentioned procurement and security earlier — can you loop them in so we have everyone on the call?

Proposed times (PST):
- Thu 2026-02-12 09:00–09:45
- Thu 2026-02-12 13:00–13:45
- Fri 2026-02-13 10:00–10:45

Agenda (30–45 min):
1) Quick recap of test harness and config (SE)
2) Latency & throughput results + anomalies (SE)
3) Open questions for security/prod
4) Procurement next steps and timeline

I’ve cc’d Dev (our SE) and Stephanie (solutions lead). If none of the proposed times work, let us know a few windows and we’ll reschedule. I’ll attach the preliminary results ahead of the call.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the note and for the CSV. We definitely want the readout. Please include Priya from procurement and Carlos from security; I’ve cc’d them. A couple constraints from our side: Priya is only available after 11am PST on Thursday, and Carlos has a standing leadership review from 12:30–13:30. The DevOps team would prefer early morning or late afternoon so they can be on the call without missing the daily deploy window.

Best windows for our group (PST):
- Thu 2026-02-12 11:15–12:00 (works for Priya, but Carlos may have a conflict)
- Thu 2026-02-12 15:00–15:45 (Carlos free, DevOps might be tight)
- Fri 2026-02-13 10:00–10:45 (preferred by DevOps & Carlos)

If you can do Fri 10am that would be the easiest to get all stakeholders. If you can’t, we can do Thu 11:15 and Carlos will dial in for the first 25 minutes and then we’ll record.

—Alex

Hey all —

Thanks for the context, Alex. Quick notes from the SE side:
- I can run through the exact test harness we used (model, tokenization, context length, batching, and KV cache behavior).
- The attached CSV is the export from our internal harness; I also put together a short summary PDF with the high-level latency percentiles and the workload shape we saw.
- For the readout, it would help if Acme can confirm the exact workload (avg prompt length, peak concurrent requests) so we can map the numbers to expected production SLOs.

Agenda suggestion (30–45 min):
1) Test setup + config (5–7 min)
2) Results walkthrough (p50/p90/p99, tail variance) (12–15 min)
3) Q&A: security and procurement asks (10–15 min)
4) Next steps: procurement timeline and dedicated sizing (5 min)

I’m available Thu after 10:30, Fri morning, and most of next week. I’ll also attach the summary PDF.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
